rules_file_note: The rules file is 1 byte (a single newline): it contains no tasks, diagnosis rules or priority evaluations. Every verdict below is therefore judged against an empty rule set.

elements.problem: Section header of a treatment box ('Treat the HIV positive patient in labour'). It names the population (HIV positive, in labour) but states no criterion, threshold, diagnosis or priority; the house standard turns a red box into check_for/priority rules only when it is a 'give urgent attention' box, which this is not.
Administrative note about filling 'C#DELIVERY' on the blood request form. No clinical logic.

Three parts, all management: (1) continue ART through delivery, (2) check viral load regardless of when last done, (3) review the result at the 3-6 day postnatal visit. The 'If on ART' condition selects a treatment path, not a diagnosis or priority. Manage tasks are out of scope by design.
Drug dosing: single-dose NVP 200mg plus single-dose TLD (TDF/3TC/DTG 300/300/50mg) for the patient not on ART. The 'If not on ART' condition selects a treatment, not a diagnosis or priority.

Timing of the drug administration above ('ideally during early labour, urgently if delivery is imminent'). The word 'urgently' qualifies when to give the dose, not the patient's triage priority, so it does not justify a priority evaluation.
Start ART next day (cross-reference to page 126) and give a 2-month supply. Management and cross-reference only.

'Decide HIV transmission risk of HIV-exposed baby' is a risk assessment, but the criteria live entirely on page 186; this page only points there and the resulting action (infant prophylaxis) is management of the neonate, outside the adult rule set.
Abbreviation key (DTG, FTC, NVP, TDF, 3TC, TLD). No clinical logic.

elements.scope_reason: Almost all of this block is treatment (calcium, aspirin, Tdap, influenza vaccine, methyldopa, weekly review, referral at 38 weeks, ART/PrEP). One part carries triage-like logic: 'If gestational hypertension ... If proteinuria/new symptoms, refer urgently.' That is a conditional urgent referral, which other pages encode as a priority evaluation. Against: it sits inside a treatment list, the criteria are not spelled out here (the weekly review and the proteinuria criteria are delegated to page 179), and the house standard derives priority rules from 'give urgent attention' red boxes, which this page does not have. The Hb >= 10 / < 10 iron dosing thresholds are management and in any case not_representable (Hb has no unit in the language). The aspirin risk list (hypertension, diabetes, SLE, antiphospholipid syndrome, previous pre-eclampsia) is a treatment indication, not a diagnosis.
parts_missing: If gestational hypertension and proteinuria or new symptoms -> refer urgently (the only candidate for an Urgent priority evaluation on this page; nothing in the file)
elements.problem: Nothing is encoded. If the project treats 'refer urgently' lines inside treatment sections as priority logic, an Urgent evaluation on (and gestational hypertension (or proteinuria, new symptoms)) is missing; if page 179 already carries that logic, nothing is lost here. All other parts of the block are management steps and correctly absent.

rule_level_problems.problem: The rules file is empty (one newline). That is consistent with the page, which has no 'give urgent attention' box, no 'X likely' or 'consider X' statement and no flowchart; the house standard requires a .lisp only when there is triage or diagnostic logic. But an empty file is indistinguishable from a build that silently failed, so the pipeline should confirm the builders deliberately produced no rules rather than crashing.

rule_level_problems.rule: (absent) Urgent: gestational hypertension with proteinuria or new symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: The one line on the page that reads as triage ('If proteinuria/new symptoms, refer urgently') has no rule. Whether it belongs here or on page 179 (where the weekly review and its criteria are defined) is a judgment call; it should be settled once across the antenatal pages so the referral is encoded exactly once.

summary: The rules file is empty, and that is largely justified: page 181 is advice, treatment, a review schedule and a treatment box for the HIV-positive patient in labour, with no urgent-attention box, no 'X likely' and no flowchart, so all eight red-box elements are out of scope (management steps, notes, cross-references). The one borderline item is the outside line 'If gestational hypertension ... if proteinuria/new symptoms, refer urgently', which is not encoded; it probably belongs to page 179 but should be assigned deliberately. The pipeline should confirm the empty file was an intentional 'no logic' result rather than a failed build.
